verdict.rationale: Stripe's ACP page states the protocol is 'open source and community-designed under the Apache 2.0 license' and that 'businesses can implement the specification to transact with any AI agent or payment processor' with no gate to read/implement — this directly matches the story. A community comment also frames MPP as a serious protocol submitted to IETF, suggesting a formal spec track. However, the evidence never shows an explicit version number/changelog for the spec, and other Stripe agentic-commerce pieces (ACS, custom checkout, OCA) are waitlist/private-preview gated, which could confuse whether 'the protocol' itself is open vs. Stripe's commercial product wrapping it. missing for 10: explicit spec versioning/changelog evidence, independent hands-on confirmation of unrestricted spec access, clarity that ACP openness isn't undercut by ChatGPT-participation application gating.
